subject: RE: Business case discussion
text:
Hey Mahaveer and Hema,

Just bringing this conversation together.

It's becoming clear that Clutterbot will struggle to scale quickly with
current data ops tools. When we look at what's been covered so far, a few
themes have emerged:

*1) SV doesn't handle massive datasets well *- Encord has been built for
companies that scale. Our clients often have 100's of annotators, very busy
scenes with 100's of objects and simple ingestion of millions of images /
video's.

*2) You need to optimise your workforce -* Encords analytics suite enables
clients to track the time spent on each task, label and project. This
functionality is key when managing and optimising the work of 100+
annotators.

*3) Video unlocks massive efficiency gains in annotation - *Encord is
purpose built for video native rendering. Clutterbot is spending up to 60
mins per frame due to the many objects in each frame. Our automatic
tracking means that each label can be applied to up to 150 frames. We have
seen 10X efficiency gains when working with teams when moving from frame
only to video tracking.

*4) Better data, not more data  *- Encords curation and model eval modules
will change the way Clutterbot prioritises data for annotation. Curation
enables teams to find the best scenes to send for labelling, removing
duplicates and bad quality images. And the eval module helps AI teams to
spot the problems quickly (comparing model predictions to ground truths)
and prioritise the collection and labelling of these areas where the model
is lacking context.

Outside of this, incorporating agents, speeding up review and managing data
pipelines automatically have all come up as potential wins. This case study
